newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to get regular economic briefing Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to get regular economic briefing Tuesday.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters on Tuesday that President Bill Clinton would receive his regular weekly economic briefing from his top economic advisers on Tuesday morning.

The spokesman added that to his knowledge the president does not receive any advance warning of possible interest rate moves by the Federal Reserve Board. The Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee started a regularly scheduled meeting at 9 a.m. EST (1400 GMT) on Tuesday.

"The president's got his weekly economic briefing with (Council of Economic Advisers Chairman) Janet Yellen," McCurry said, adding the meeting was at 1120 EST (1620 GMT). "They talk about trends in the economy and economic statistics."

He said others at the briefing include Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, Chairman of the National Economic Council Gene Sperling and Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines.
He said the meeting did not include anyone from the Fed. Asked if the president receives advance warning of Fed interest rate moves, McCurry replied: "Not to my knowledge."
